ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two separated organic fragments in the figure, with several curved arrows; the problem requires ignoring these arrows. The upper fragment is an enolate skeleton: the left side is an R-substituted alkene carbon, and the right alkene carbon is connected to R1 and a negatively charged O. The lower fragment is a carbonyl skeleton: the carbonyl carbon is connected to R3 and R2, and is double-bonded to O. Reasoning: The upper skeleton can be written as R-CH=C(O-)-R1, and after using wildcards to represent substituents it is */C=C(/*)[O-]. The lower carbonyl R3-C(=O)-R2 is represented with wildcards as *C(*)=O. Since they are separated fragments in the figure, SMILES connects them with a dot, so the result is */C=C(/*)[O-].*C(*)=O.

method.method_draft: First visually transcribe only the skeleton in the figure and ignore all curved arrows. The upper species is R-CH=C(O-)-R1, so write it as a wildcard-substituted alkene with the negatively charged oxygen on the right alkene carbon: */C=C(/*)[O-]. The lower species is a ketone/aldehyde-like carbonyl R3-C(=O)-R2, represented with wildcards as *C(*)=O. Since the image shows these as separate fragments, join their SMILES with a dot to obtain */C=C(/*)[O-].*C(*)=O.
